run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The user-facing failure in namespace hotel-reservation is HTTP 500 on frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels', and it traces down the chain frontend -> search -> rate. The deepest observable fault is inside the rate service: its own request admission control is saturated. Its own metric snapshot (scraped ~04:51:15Z) shows rate_backend_qps_limit=20, rate_queue_capacity=256 and rate_queue_depth=256 (the queue pinned at capacity), with rate_requests_received_total=1243, rate_requests_completed_total=491, rate_requests_rejected_total=496 and rate_requests_expired_total=135 since process start, and rate_in_flight=0. Its '/rate.Rate/GetRates' server spans confirm this: 843 of 2283 spans in the sampled period ended after more than 10 s (sample spans 12.709-12.798 s, close to the 256/20 = 12.8 s a full 256-slot queue represents at a 20/s limit), and the only downstream child span, memcached_get_multi_rate (325-628 us), starts at the END of that wait - so the time is spent inside rate before its only dependency call, not in memcached or mongo. rate also returns 842 immediate error spans (11-800 us) which match the queue-full rejection path. The rate pod is not resource-bound (0.068 CPU cores against a 1-core limit, 21.7 MB working set, no CPU-throttling series for that pod), and memcached-rate/mongodb-rate/geo/profile/reservation show no error spans and normal latency, so throttling is configured, not resource-driven. Downstream effects with their own evidence: search's client spans to rate are ~750 ms (matching RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, up to 3 attempts per RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3), search logged 'downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded/ResourceExhausted' continuously 04:51:45-04:51:57Z, its own counters show 1473 rate attempts for 733 search requests with 435 timeouts and 368 failures, and frontend emitted 723 error spans with http.status_code=500 on GET /hotels. Caveats: there is no healthy baseline - the entire environment (all namespaces) was created at 2026-11-24T04:49:58Z and Jaeger holds no earlier traces; the application /metrics endpoints were unscrapable (up=0) until ~04:51:00-04:51:15Z, so the rate/search counters are a single snapshot, not a reliable time series.

claims.text: All 19 hotel-reservation Deployments report 1/1 ready replicas and all 19 pods are Running with restartCount 0, every pod created 2026-11-24T04:49:58Z; every Deployment object's last kubectl-client-side-apply write is 2026-11-24T04:49:58Z, i.e. the application was (re)deployed as a whole at the end of the authorized window and no later object change is recorded.

The Deployment 'rate' (hotel-reservation) holds the admission-control settings in its container env: RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (only other env is JAEGER_SAMPLE_RATIO=1), with image ghcr.io/sregym/hotel-reservation@sha256:1c685e1c..., CPU request 100m / limit 1.

The Deployment 'search' (hotel-reservation) holds the rate-call client settings in its container env: RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=50, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0, RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2.

rate's own metrics (instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091) at the sampled instant show rate_backend_qps_limit=20, rate_queue_capacity=256, rate_queue_depth=256 (queue exactly at capacity), rate_in_flight=0, rate_requests_received_total=1243, rate_requests_completed_total=491, rate_requests_rejected_total=496 and rate_requests_expired_total=135.

search's own metrics (instance search.hotel-reservation:9092) at the same sampled instant show search_requests_total=733 but search_rate_attempts_total=1473, search_rate_successes_total=356, search_rate_failures_total=368 and search_rate_timeouts_total=435, i.e. about two rate attempts per search request.

rate's '/rate.Rate/GetRates' span durations are extremely long: of 2283 spans in the histogram, 1440 are <=10000 ms and 2283 total, so 843 spans exceed 10 s; individual spans in the trace sample last 12.709-12.798 s, and in each of them the child span 'memcached_get_multi_rate' (duration 325-628 us) starts only at the end of the parent span, so the wait happens inside rate before its only downstream call.

rate itself also returns errors: 842 of its '/rate.Rate/GetRates' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and the error-tagged ones in the trace sample are immediate (11-800 us), consistent with rejection rather than slow work.

search's application log for pod search-7769dfc66b-dwrwk records repeated 'downstream request failed dependency=rate grpc_code=DeadlineExceeded' and '... grpc_code=ResourceExhausted' warnings from 2026-11-24T04:51:45Z through 04:51:57Z (100 newest matching lines shown, 792 matching lines in the window).

search's client spans to rate ('/rate.Rate/GetRates' with service_name=search) last about 750 ms (750,044-750,823 us), matching RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750, and failed search requests carry 2-3 such attempts (e.g. trace 3a6bd88ad7450557 has attempts at 04:51:56.242, 04:51:57.038 and 04:51:57.129 while the parent '/search.Search/Nearby' span fails).

frontend is failing user requests on its own: its 'HTTP GET /hotels' spans carry error=true with http.status_code=500 (723 error spans vs 356 without error status, durations 0.88-1.65 s), its child '/search.Search/Nearby' spans are error, and error-status ('STATUS_CODE_ERROR') series exist only for frontend, rate and search - not for geo, profile or reservation.

The rate pod rate-c4d7bcb48-rzt7p is not resource-starved: CPU usage 0.068 cores against a 1-core limit, working set 21.7 MB, restartCount 0, and no CPU-throttling series exists for it (the only container_cpu_cfs throttling ratios returned were consul and mongodb-recommendation, both 0).

rate's dependencies and the other services on the paths are healthy in the same period: memcached-rate pod memcached-rate-5b59cb5d9d-gj6qm is Running with 0 restarts and 0.012 cores, 'memcached_get_multi_rate' spans take only 325-628 us, rate's 'mongo_rate' internal spans (5 of them) carry no error status, geo server spans take 34-68 us, profile's memcached span ~0.5 ms, and geo/profile/reservation have no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series at all.

No other object applies this setting or a fault to rate: the hotel-reservation namespace has 0 NetworkPolicies, and the only ConfigMaps in hotel-reservation are kube-root-ca.crt, mongo-geo-script and mongo-rate-script - no ConfigMap holds any RATE_* setting, so RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT/RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY exist only in the rate Deployment.

The Deployment 'rate' is where the fault originates: its admission-control configuration (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=20 with RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256) is permanently saturated - rate_queue_depth=256=capacity, 496 of 1243 received requests rejected, 135 expired, only 491 completed - and its GetRates handler blocks ~12.7-12.8 s internally before its only dependency call, while the container uses 0.068 CPU cores of a 1-core limit, so the loss of throughput is the configured limit/queue rather than resource exhaustion.

Unrelated to this chain: pod mongodb-profile-758cb77f9f-mqgzv got one FailedScheduling event at 04:49:58Z ('persistentvolumeclaim "profile-pvc" not found') during initial scheduling; the profile path shows no error spans, so this startup event is not tied to the frontend/rate failure.

Mechanism: with rate_backend_qps_limit=20 and rate_queue_capacity=256, a full queue implies a maximum stay of 256/20 = 12.8 s, which matches the observed 12.709-12.798 s GetRates spans; requests therefore wait the whole queue (memcached is called only afterwards), the queue stays at capacity, about 40% of arrivals are rejected immediately (ResourceExhausted) and requests whose caller has already given up are still processed, so callers see deadline timeouts.

Second candidate cause: search's client policy (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=750 with RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3) both converts rate's queueing into hard failures and roughly doubles the load delivered to rate (1473 attempts for 733 search requests, 435 timeouts), which can by itself keep rate's 256-slot queue above its 20/s admission limit; if the rate limit were sized for un-retried demand (~9 frontend requests/s), this retry amplification would be the trigger that saturates it.

Rejected: rate is slow because of CPU throttling or memory pressure - its container used 0.068 CPU cores of a 1-core limit, 21.7 MB working set, restarted 0 times, and no container_cpu_cfs throttling series was returned for it.

Rejected: rate is slow because memcached-rate or mongodb-rate is slow/failing - memcached_get_multi_rate spans completed in 325-628 us with no error status, mongo_rate spans carried no error status, and both pods (memcached-rate-5b59cb5d9d-gj6qm, mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-bmxrw) are Running with 0 restarts.

Size rate's admission control for the real peak demand and the retry behaviour: raise RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT (and/or increase drain throughput) above peak offered GetRates rate so rate_queue_depth stops sitting at rate_queue_capacity, and align search's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS / RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS with the worst-case time a request can spend in rate's queue (a 750 ms deadline against a ~12.8 s queue hold guarantees timeouts and a retry storm). Alert on rate_queue_depth/rate_queue_capacity and rate_requests_rejected_total, which moved first.

gaps: No healthy baseline: the entire environment was created at 2026-11-24T04:49:58Z, Jaeger holds no traces before ~04:50-04:51Z, and the whole window's traffic is post-deployment, so I cannot compare against normal RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT/RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY values or prove when/how the settings deviated from default.

The application /metrics endpoints were unscrapable until the scrape at ~04:51:00Z (search) / ~04:51:15Z (rate) (up=0 before), and the rate/search counters I cite appear identical across the later 15 s samples, which I cannot explain (source_start_at of the app-metric views is 04:51:05/04:51:15); counter deltas and the exact fill/decline of rate_queue_depth over time are therefore unreliable and I only use the snapshot values.
Change history integration is not configured for this Run, so I cannot confirm which actor applied the rate/search env values or whether an earlier value existed.

The internal accounting of rate's admission control (why only 491 requests completed while its limit is 20/s, and whether rejections, expirations and completions overlap) is not observable from the metrics exposed; rate's application log contains only startup lines (04:49:59-04:50:08Z) and no per-request or error lines.

A cluster-wide query of customresourcedefinitions filtered on names matching chaos|fault|inject returned nothing (that view's status was no_data, so it is recorded here rather than cited as evidence that no such CRD exists); likewise no job objects exist in any namespace.
user, recommendation and consul services produced no spans or app metrics in the query window and are not on the observed failing path, so their health is unchecked rather than confirmed.

No alert state at the incident-window end is available (Prometheus rules were read at 04:54-04:55Z, after the authorized window); the firing HighRequestLatency (rate p95 10,000 ms) and HighRequestErrorRate (search 80.01%, frontend 100%) alerts are post-window observations only.
next_steps: Confirm with the owners what the intended (non-fault) values of RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY, RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS and RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS are for this deployment, since the sandbox has no pre-incident baseline.

Plot rate_queue_depth, rate_requests_rejected_total and rate_requests_expired_total over a longer period once the /metrics endpoints are continuously scrapable, to confirm the queue is permanently at capacity rather than sampled at a burst.

If rate's limit is intended to be protective rather than the fault, test the alternative branch by aligning search's rate-call timeout/attempts with rate's worst-case queue hold before changing the rate limit.

data.k8s-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
